subject: Data transfer mapping and UK IDTA alignment for upcoming PoC
messages:
From: Sam Kowalski <sam.kowalski@northbayhealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: NorthBay Legal <legal@northbayhealth.com>
Date: Sun, 19 Mar 2028 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: Data transfer mapping and UK IDTA alignment for upcoming PoC

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for the run-through on Friday. As we scope the proof-of-concept (PoC) for our integration I need to close a few data transfer and DPA items before we go live for testing. Quick list of asks so your team can triage: 

- Complete list of subprocessors (including roles and regions) that will process NHS/UK patient data for the PoC.
- A copy of how you map the EU SCCs to the UK IDTA / UK Addendum (any equivalence table or narrative).
- High-level TIA/DTIA summary describing where exports occur and mitigations.
- Confirmation of KMS/HSM use (where keys are located, access policies).
- Logging/retention: sample of token-level access logs or a description of what you retain and for how long.

We have a tight timeline: PoC begins April 10, so legal needs anything that requires DocuSign by April 3. If you can send material or an attestation that would be ideal. I attached a short scope doc with our questions.

Also flagging a sensitive subprocessor: Telemetry Inc — our security team will want to know whether they see raw PII or only telemetry hashes.

Can we get an initial bundle by next Friday (Mar 24)? If helpful we can do a 30-minute call next week to walk through.

Appreciate it,

Sam Kowalski
VP, IT Security
NorthBay Health
(sam.kowalski@northbayhealth.com)

Attachment: NBH-DPA-Scope-questions.docx

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Sam Kowalski <sam.kowalski@northbayhealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 19 Mar 2028 17:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Data transfer mapping and UK IDTA alignment for upcoming PoC

Sam — thanks for the clear checklist. We can cover everything you listed; summary below and proposed timelines.

Quick answers / next steps:
- Subprocessors: we will produce a CSV export with roles, country of processing, and whether the subprocessed data includes PII. We will flag Telemetry Inc and provide a usage note.
- SCC -> UK IDTA mapping: we will send a mapping PDF that shows clause-by-clause equivalence and whether we rely on the UK Addendum for specific clauses.
- TIA/DTIA: short (2–3 page) summary for the PoC scope; we will call out transfers, legal mechanisms, and technical mitigations.
- KMS/HSM: confirm HSM-backed key management (multi-tenant model with customer-keying options); provide whitepaper and access control matrix.
- Logging: provide examples of the types of logs retained, retention windows, and an anonymized sample. We don't retain raw PII in request caching.

Proposed timeline:
- Mar 24: initial package (subprocessors CSV + SCCs->UK mapping + TIA summary).
- Mar 27: 30-minute drop-in call to review and take questions (we can share screen and walk the mapping).
- Apr 3: DocuSign-ready UK IDTA addendum if required.

Attachments we will include in the package: redwood_subprocessors_2028-03.csv, sccs_to_ukidta_mapping_2028-03-22.pdf, TIA_summary_NBH_PoC_2028-03-22.pdf.

If NorthBay legal needs wording changes to the addendum we can circulate redlines; Jonas will own technical details during the call and Kimberly will coordinate legal/docsign cadence.

On process: are you expecting an attestation letter (signed) or a simple package and DocuSign addendum? Leaning on the attestation is faster for PoC but I want to align to your procurement process.

Thanks — sending to our compliance queue now and we should hit the Mar 24 delivery date.

From: Sam Kowalski <sam.kowalski@northbayhealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Mar 2028 08:34:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Data transfer mapping and UK IDTA alignment for upcoming PoC

Rachel — quick follow-ups before your package: 

- For logs, our security team specifically needs token-level access traces that show which Redwood human or service principal requested a record and from which AWS region. Will you be able to provide a sanitized sample log that preserves the attribute shapes we need?
- For Telemetry Inc: please indicate whether they ever process unredacted PII for troubleshooting; if they do, we will need specific contractual limitations or an alternate routing.
- Are there any US-based subprocessors that will process UK-origin data? If so, list which subprocessors and what safeguards you apply (e.g., binding contracts, encryption-in-transit, onshore proxies).

Finally, can you point me to the DocuSign link for the UK addendum when it's ready? Legal prefers a single addendum signed by both sides.

Cheers,
Sam

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Sam Kowalski <sam.kowalski@northbayhealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 15:40:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Data transfer mapping and UK IDTA alignment for upcoming PoC

Sam — thanks, good questions. Our package is attached and below are the precise answers your team requested. If anything needs more depth we can follow up on the call Mar 27.

Attachments (in Drive + attached to this email):
- redwood_subprocessors_2028-03.csv (roles, processing countries, data subset flag for PII)
- sccs_to_ukidta_mapping_2028-03-22.pdf (clause mapping and notes)
- TIA_summary_NBH_PoC_2028-03-22.pdf (DTIA highlights and mitigations)

Direct answers:
- Logs: we can provide a sanitized sample that preserves field names/timestamps, service principal IDs, and region tags. We do not publish raw patient identifiers in logs; we can show event IDs + hashed request identifiers to demonstrate access lineage. Sample will be in the Drive folder.
- Telemetry Inc: Telemetry is used for aggregated monitoring and receives only telemetry hashes and metrics. They do not receive raw PII for the PoC. We included a note in the subprocessors CSV with that limitation and the contractual restriction.
- US-based subprocessors: there are two optional US processors used for analytics (AnalyticsCo US and QueueWorks). For PoC traffic by default we will route UK-origin traffic to EU/UK regions; where processing in the US cannot be avoided (e.g., analytics sampling), we apply encryption-in-transit, strict ACLs, and contractual SCC-based flow restrictions. This is documented in the TIA summary.
- KMS/HSM: Redwood uses HSM-backed KMS for tenant keys; keys are logically separated per-tenant. For customers that require customer-controlled keys we offer bring-your-own-key (BYOK) options.

DocuSign / next steps:
- UK IDTA addendum draft is uploaded to the Drive folder. If you confirm 'attestation + addendum' flow we will route the addendum for signature and expect completion by Apr 3 if there are no redlines. DocuSign link (placeholder) is: https://www.docusign.com/signed/uk-idta-addendum-example
- We will host a 30-minute review call on Mar 27 at 09:00 UTC. Jonas will present the technical mapping; Kimberly will run legal/DocuSign items.

Let me know if you'd like a supplemental attestation letter signed by Redwood's CPO/GC for the PoC; we can prepare that in parallel.

Thanks — attaching package and sharing Drive link now.

Rachel Kim
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
(rachel.kim@redwood.com)

--
Attachment stubs: redwood_subprocessors_2028-03.csv (text/csv), sccs_to_ukidta_mapping_2028-03-22.pdf (application/pdf), TIA_summary_NBH_PoC_2028-03-22.pdf (application/pdf)
